name: Corporate Enforcer
description: Elites trained in smart-linked firearms, monomolecular blades, and tactical neural reflex boosters for close-quarters warfare.

multiclass_prerequisites.description: 2024 multiclass prerequisite: meet this class primary ability requirement when adding a new class; requirements also apply to every current class.

armor: Light, Medium, and Heavy armor and Shields

choices.name: Choose starting skills
choices.eligibility_rule: Choose distinct skills; verify handling of an already-proficient skill.
choices.selection_effect: Record proficiency in the selected skills.

multiclass_proficiencies.description: Gain the following traits from the Core Fighter Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields.

starting_equipment.description: Choose A, B, or C: (A) Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, 8 Javelins, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 4 GP; (B) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or (C) 155 GP Starting equipment is not granted on multiclass entry.

choices.eligibility_rule: Choose one listed bundle when starting as this class.

resources.name: Nanite Repair Injection
resources.description:
See the Second Wind feature for costs, use, and recovery. You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.
resources.maximum_rule: See the feature and level table; resolve structured maximum and recovery rules before implementation.

resources.name: Synaptic Overclock
resources.description:
See the Action Surge feature for costs, use, and recovery. You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.
resources.maximum_rule: See the feature and level table; resolve structured maximum and recovery rules before implementation.

resources.name: Neural Hardening
resources.description:
See the Indomitable feature for costs, use, and recovery. If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

You can use this feature twice before a Long Rest starting at level 13 and three times before a Long Rest starting at level 17.

features.name: Combat Augment Protocol (Fighting Style)
features.description:
You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see “Feats”). Defense is recommended.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

choices.name: Choose a Fighting Style feat
choices.allowed_options: Eligible Fighting Style feats; Paladin and Ranger may instead select their cantrip-granting option described in the feature.
choices.eligibility_rule: Meet feat prerequisites and apply any replacement rule in the feature.

reskin_reference.name: 1. Combat Augment Protocol (Level 1)
reskin_reference.description: You calibrate your neural interface and physical sub-dermal augments for a specific combat doctrine:

features.name: Smart Link Targeting
features.description: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls made with ranged smart-weapons and firearms.

features.name: Sub Dermal Plating
features.description: You gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing armor or sub-dermal weave.

features.name: Monomolecular Edge Tuning
features.description: When wielding a one-handed melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls.

features.name: Hydraulic Torque Drive
features.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack with a two-handed weapon, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

features.name: Hard Light Aegis Intercept
features.description: When a target within 5 feet of you is attacked, you can use your reaction to project a hard-light barrier, imposing disadvantage on the attack roll (requires a shield or cyber-shield).

features.name: Dual Rotor Actuators
features.description: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

features.name: Nanite Repair Injection (Second Wind)
features.description:
You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

reskin_reference.name: 2. Nanite Repair Injection (Level 1)
reskin_reference.description: You activate a sub-dermal auto-injector or trigger a nanite repair swarm that instantly cauterizes wounds, seals flesh, and numbs trauma.

features.name: Mechanics
features.description: On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 + your Fighter level. (1/Short or Long Rest).

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

choices.name: Choose weapon masteries
choices.allowed_options: Eligible weapon kinds as described by the feature.
choices.eligibility_rule: Follow proficiency, weapon type, and replacement restrictions in the source feature.

features.name: Class progression values
features.description: Second Wind: 2; Weapon Mastery: 3. These are totals at this class level, not additional grants.

features.name: Synaptic Overclock (Action Surge)
features.description:
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

reskin_reference.name: 3. Synaptic Overclock (Level 2)
reskin_reference.description: You temporarily override your neural safety governors or trigger a heavy combat-stim dump, allowing your body to move at near-light reaction speeds.

features.name: Mechanics
features.description: On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and possible bonus action. (1/Short or Long Rest; 2 uses at Level 17).

features.name: Tactical Mind
features.description: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.

source_notes: Rules basis: _reference/classes/Fighter.md, a 2024-style source. Review compatibility with the earlier 2014 multiclass design.
Class progression and mechanics use the original reference; older reskin mechanics may differ and are thematic reference only, not additional grants.
The worksheet schema is not supported by the app. Levels remain unfilled pending rules and choice review; null means unresolved or not applicable as described.
Subclass selection milestones are recorded, but subclass options, features, and spellcasting are intentionally deferred.
Reskin inspiration: classes/Corporate Enforcer.json. Names may be adapted where source mechanics have changed.
Separate from the existing Barbarian-based Corporate Enforcer worksheet; this worksheet uses Fighter rules.
